newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia June trade data to include gold sale. [CORRECTED 2:53 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Australia June trade data to include gold sale. [CORRECTED 2:53 GMT]

text.p: Australia's balance of goods and services data for June, to be released on July 29, will include the Reserve Bank of Australia's sale of some its gold reserves, the Bureau of Statistics said on Friday.

On July 4, the central bank announced it had sold some 167 tonnes of gold in the preceeding six months worth around A$2.3 billion. The ABS said the change of ownership of 125 tonnes of gold would be taken in June as an export and the rest in August and September.
(Corrects to make clear that not all 167 tonnes of gold sold would be included in June data).
That meant the balance of goods would show a huge surplus, which analysts estimated at around A$2.0 billion or more, which would easily be the largest on record.
Australia's total exports in May amounted to A$9.232 billion and the balance of goods and services was in surplus to the tune of A$873 million.
